title: Persistent sessions owned by a server
body:
A decade session should outlive its window and mostly survive a reboot. Today every pane is a Wayland client of the decade process, and closing the window ends decade and every program in it.

Jack's requirement, from 2026-11-07: a server owns the session and its panes, a window only views it, and the layout and each pane's cwd come back after a reboot. herdr's session model was the starting reference. Jack kept only the server-owned, persistent part of it and dropped herdr's agent detection and sidebar.

Pieces, each its own issue:

- how the server and its viewers are split, and how frames and input travel between them
- the session directory, names, and the commands that start, attach to, list and stop a session
- saving the session and restoring it at server start
- remote viewing, over the network
